note: Latest Home Office Immigration system statistics release is year ending March 2026 (published 21 May 2026). Asylum appeals come from a separate publisher (HMCTS/Ministry of Justice tribunals statistics, January to March 2026). Reference periods differ between measures, so do not mix calendar-year, year-ending, and point-in-time figures.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum applications (people claiming asylum)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people claim asylum in the UK?
metrics.notes: Counts people (main applicants and dependants). Down 21% on the year ending June 2025. The Home Office states the high was 109,662 in the year ending September 2025.

metrics.metric_name: People claiming asylum, calendar year 2025
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, Asylum summary tables, table Asy_00a
metrics.notes: PEOPLE, main applicants plus dependants. A calendar year, so it does not line up with the year-ending-June figures used elsewhere on this site. Held twice deliberately: it is also the 2025 point of the asylum applications series, and series_ref keeps the two from drifting. It exists as a metric because Markdown pages cannot cite a series point and two of them were rounding it to 100,000 longhand. The year ending June 2026 edition revised this year from 100,625 to 101,911.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum claims from unaccompanied asylum-seeking children
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people claim asylum in the UK?
metrics.notes: A FLOW, and it exists on this site to answer a question a stock cannot. The asylum support total excludes unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, who are supported by local authorities, and NO UK-WIDE COUNT OF THOSE CHILDREN IN LOCAL AUTHORITY CARE IS PUBLISHED BESIDE IT: the Home Office's support tables exclude them by definition, and the looked-after-children statistics that do count them are published by the Department for Education for England alone, so they are not comparable in geography with a United Kingdom support figure. This is what the publisher does state, claims made in the year rather than children being supported on a date, and it must not be read as the missing queue. The Home Office puts it at 5% of all claims in the same period. Added 10 August 2026.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum applications, main applicants (cases requiring a decision)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, Asylum summary tables, table Asy_01a
metrics.notes: Main-applicant total (excludes dependants); the count of asylum cases requiring Home Office consideration. 69,848 main applicants within 85,891 people, a 20% decrease on the previous 12 months. RE-SOURCED FROM THE COMMONS LIBRARY TO THE HOME OFFICE ON 3 AUGUST 2026: the Library rounds this figure and prints no exact one, while table Asy_01a prints it in the same row-block as the people total this site already publishes. That move changed neither the value nor the grade, only the citation.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum initial decision grant rate
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people are granted asylum in the UK?
metrics.notes: Proportion of initial decisions (main applicants) resulting in a grant of protection or other leave; excludes withdrawals and administrative outcomes. Down from 49% a year earlier; peak was 77% (year ending September 2022). This site's rule, not a Home Office instruction: do not add a cohort uplift to this rate. The Home Office puts the grant rate at the latest outcome 17 to 29 percentage points above the initial rate for each year of claim between 2007 and 2020. That range belongs to the detailed cohort analysis Asy_D04, which covers claims made from 2007 and is what the bulletin cites under Figure 4; the summary table Asy_04 presents the same analysis from 2010 onwards, names Asy_D04 as its own source, and is where note 48 sits, saying that table's initial rate "will not match the grant rate in the 'initial decisions' dataset as they relate to a different cohort of initial decisions". Do not attach the 2007 window to Asy_04, which does not reach back that far. The publisher attributes the gap to appeals and reconsiderations. Asy_04's note 46 separately records that claims withdrawn or given an administrative outcome may later be reinstated and given a substantive outcome; reading that as a third route into the later figure is this site's inference and not a link the publisher draws. The Home Office's terms for the later figure are 'latest outcome' and 'latest decision'; it does not call it final. Two publisher caveats sit on Asy_D04: its note 4 says outcomes are as at January 2026, and its note 5 says appeals data was not available at extraction for this release, because immigration data is moving to a new caseworking system. The bulletin dates the same outcomes to April 2026 instead. January is followed here, being the date the cohort table publishes for itself and the earlier of the two, so this record claims no more currency than the publisher's own table does.

metrics.metric_name: People granted protection or other leave at initial decision
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people are granted asylum in the UK?
metrics.notes: Includes main applicants and dependants. Down 21% on the previous year. Of 115,872 people who received an initial decision, 73,478 were refused (up 23%).

metrics.metric_name: Asylum backlog, people awaiting an initial decision
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people are in the UK asylum system?
metrics.notes: Relates to 32,401 cases. Down 56% on June 2025, which is this site's arithmetic; the Home Office states separately that it is the lowest level since June 2019 and down 77% from the June 2023 peak, which is held as its own record rather than restated here. A point-in-time stock figure.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum backlog, cases awaiting an initial decision
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people are in the UK asylum system?
metrics.notes: Cases are main applicants only. The 40,168 people awaiting an initial decision relate to these 32,401 cases.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum backlog, highest number of people awaiting an initial decision
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people are in the UK asylum system?
metrics.notes: THIS IS A MAXIMUM, SO RE-DERIVE IT AT EVERY RELEASE RATHER THAN CARRYING IT FORWARD. The Home Office states it as a peak in its own words on the release page, which is why this record cites that page rather than the summary table: the asylum summary table this site charts from publishes year-end columns only and cannot show a June figure at all. It is deliberately not declared in table_reference here, because this value is not read from it. That is the same shape as the ONS peaks in migration.json, and it is why the chart on /asylum/ says the within-year peak was higher than either line shows.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum backlog, people awaiting an initial decision, end of 2019
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, Asylum summary tables, table Asy_00a
metrics.notes: The starting point of the rise the everyone-in-asylum-accommodation-arrived-recently claim page describes, and the last year-end before the queue began to climb steeply. Held as a record because that page is markdown and only a Nunjucks chart summary can cite a series point directly; series_ref keeps it in step with the point the chart draws. The page rounded it to about 51,000 until 2 August 2026, which collided with a different figure of the same rounding, the appeals backlog a year before the current one.

metrics.metric_name: Total asylum cases in the casework system (work in progress)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics (citing Migration Transparency Data ASY_03)
metrics.notes: Total work in progress: cases awaiting an initial decision plus those awaiting appeal or removal. NOT current, the latest full figure is June 2024 (a record high) because the wider breakdown was suspended pending a new caseworking system. Do not confuse with the current 'awaiting initial decision' figure.

metrics.metric_name: Small boat arrivals, calendar year 2025
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, Illegal entry routes summary tables, table IER_01
metrics.notes: Second-highest annual total on record; 13% higher than 2024. The peak it is second to is held as its own record rather than restated here. Finalised calendar-year total, and the Home Office states it as one: table IER_01 of the summary tables prints small boat arrivals by calendar year, 2018 to 2025, and its 2025 cell is this figure. RE-SOURCED 3 August 2026: this record previously cited the data tables index page, which lists spreadsheets and contains no figures at all, and named the detailed dataset, which publishes quarters only. The dataset was titled 'Irregular migration to the UK detailed dataset (illegal entry routes)' until the year ending December 2025 edition; the edition used here carries the current title.

metrics.metric_name: Small boat arrivals, highest calendar year on record
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, Illegal entry routes summary tables, table IER_01
metrics.notes: The highest calendar year for small boat arrivals. REGRADED FROM calculated TO official ON 3 AUGUST 2026, and the reason it was calculated was false: it read 'the Home Office publishes this dataset by quarter and states no calendar-year total', and table IER_01 prints 45,774 as a 2022 calendar-year cell, as does the Total column of IER_02a. The absolute negative was never tested, which is the failure the handoff already describes. 2025 is the second highest at 41,472, held as its own record rather than restated here.

metrics.metric_name: Small boat arrivals, year ending June 2026
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, Illegal entry routes summary tables, table IER_01
metrics.notes: Down 23% year on year, 33,374 against 43,309. 95-99% of small boat arrivals go on to claim asylum. REGRADED FROM CALCULATED TO OFFICIAL ON 27 AUGUST 2026, because the source changed shape rather than because anything was wrong. It was summed from monthly cells in the same publication while IER_01 carried calendar-year columns plus a part-year stub and printed no year-ending total; from this edition IER_01 prints a Year ending June 2026 column, so the Home Office states the figure and the derivation is retired. The share of all detected unauthorised arrivals is not stated here: the denominator is its own record and the asylum page cites both.

metrics.metric_name: Detected arrivals via illegal routes, all methods
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, Illegal entry routes summary tables, table IER_01
metrics.notes: CALCULATED, not published: table IER_01 now prints a Year ending June 2026 column but still no total row, so this is the sum of its four methods of entry: small boats 33,374, inadequately documented air arrivals 2,492, recorded detections in the UK 1,962, and recorded detections at UK ports 258. Small boats are 87.6% of it. Detected means detected: it cannot count arrivals nobody detected, so it is a floor rather than a total. RE-SOURCED ON 27 AUGUST 2026 from the detailed dataset to summary table IER_01, which is where all four components are printed together and where this figure was read.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum appeals lodged (First-tier Tribunal)
metrics.source_name: HM Courts & Tribunals Service / Ministry of Justice, Tribunals statistics quarterly, January to March 2026
metrics.notes: A single quarter's inflow, not an annual figure. MoJ table FIA_1, asylum, protection and revocation of protection receipts: 14,748 of the chamber's 27,689 in the quarter. Down from 17,822 the prior quarter, and that IS the peak rather than a possible one: 17,822 is the highest of all 76 quarters the table holds, read on 3 August 2026.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum appeals backlog (First-tier Tribunal, outstanding cases)
metrics.source_name: HM Courts & Tribunals Service / Ministry of Justice, Tribunals statistics quarterly, January to March 2026
metrics.notes: A record high. The figure a year earlier and the number of appeals disposed of in the quarter are both held as records of their own rather than restated here; between them they are why the backlog rises, because appeals lodged run at roughly twice disposals. The total open caseload of the chamber across all case types is 151,767, table FIA_4. THIS RECORD'S NOTES CLAIMED FEWER THAN 7,000 APPEALS ARE DECIDED PER QUARTER UNTIL 2 AUGUST 2026, and so did /asylum/. It was true when written and had been false for three quarters: asylum and protection disposals passed 7,000 in the July to September 2025 quarter and reached 7,799 in this one.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum appeals backlog, previous year (First-tier Tribunal, outstanding cases)
metrics.source_name: HM Courts & Tribunals Service / Ministry of Justice, Tribunals statistics quarterly, January to March 2026, table FIA_4
metrics.notes: The comparison year behind the record high above, on the precedent net-migration-2 set: a prior-year figure is republished by each release and rounding it into prose freezes a number the publisher may revise. Read from FIA_4 at 2024/25 Q4, which is the quarter ending 31 March 2025. The page rounded this to about 51,000 until 2 August 2026, which is also how the end-2019 initial-decision backlog rounds, so two unrelated queues appeared on this site as the same number.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum appeals disposed of (First-tier Tribunal)
metrics.source_name: HM Courts & Tribunals Service / Ministry of Justice, Tribunals statistics quarterly, January to March 2026, table FIA_2
metrics.notes: Asylum, protection and revocation of protection only, all disposal categories: 52% determined at a hearing or on the papers, 35% withdrawn, 6% struck out and 6% invalid or out of time. DISPOSED OF IS NOT DETERMINED, and the difference is why this record exists: 4,088 were determined, which is the base of the appeal success rate held separately, so quoting one where the other belongs understates the throughput of the tribunal by nearly half. Set beside appeals lodged in the same quarter, this is what makes the backlog rise: roughly two arrive for every one that leaves.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum appeal success (allowed) rate
metrics.source_name: HM Courts & Tribunals Service / Ministry of Justice, Tribunals statistics quarterly, January to March 2026
metrics.notes: Asylum/Protection/Revocation of Protection appeals only, MoJ table FIA_3: 4,088 determined at a hearing or on the papers in the quarter, 40% allowed. NOT a share of all disposals. Of 7,799 asylum and protection appeals disposed of, 52% were determined, 35% withdrawn, 6% struck out and 6% invalid or out of time. The chamber-wide figure across all case types is 39%, so do not mix the two. Mean time to clearance for asylum and protection, MoJ table T_3: 67 weeks; the 61 weeks in the bulletin is the chamber-wide figure. The latest quarter is provisional and the three before it have been revised.

metrics.metric_name: People in receipt of asylum support (total)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people are in the UK asylum system?
metrics.notes: In receipt of accommodation and/or subsistence support. Down 12% on June 2025 and, in the Home Office's own words, 25% below the September 2023 peak of 123,758. Excludes unaccompanied asylum-seeking children (supported by local authorities).

metrics.metric_name: People in asylum hotel accommodation
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people are in the UK asylum system?
metrics.notes: 17% of the supported population. Down 50% on June 2025 and 71% below the September 2023 peak of 56,018, both the Home Office's own comparisons. A further 78% were in other accommodation and 5% on subsistence-only support.

metrics.metric_name: People in asylum accommodation (hotel and other)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, How many people are in the UK asylum system?
metrics.notes: CALCULATED by this project as the sum of two published components: 16,021 in hotel accommodation plus 73,068 in non-hotel accommodation, including initial, contingency and dispersal. The Home Office publishes those two and the 93,293 support total, but not this sum. It is the accommodation figure, and is NOT the support total: 4,204 people received subsistence support only and are in the 93,293 but not here. Excludes unaccompanied asylum-seeking children.

metrics.metric_name: Largest nationality claiming asylum, Pakistan (share)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, table Asy_01b
metrics.notes: THE SHARE IS THIS SITE'S ARITHMETIC AND NO PUBLISHER STATES IT: Pakistan 8,305 of the 85,891 total is 9.67%, both cells printed in the Year ending June 2026 column of Asy_01b. Graded official until 3 August 2026, when the fetch found the Home Office states no share for any single nationality in this period. Pakistan is the largest named nationality, ahead of Eritrea at 6,952; the larger Other cell is a residual category rather than a nationality. The Home Office states the top six (Pakistan, Eritrea, Iran, Sudan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh) were together almost half, 46%, of claimants. Notable changes on the year: Somali claims up 64% and Sudanese up 14%; Syrian down 73% (after the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024), Vietnamese down 57% and Pakistani down 26%.

metrics.metric_name: Ukraine schemes, cumulative out-of-country visas granted
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, safe and legal (humanitarian) routes
metrics.notes: Visas granted, not arrivals (some unused). 15,595 out-of-country grants in the latest year, and a further 78,638 in-country extension grants, mostly under the Ukraine Permission Extension scheme. The release says some of those who arrived will since have left the UK and gives no figure for how many; the year ending March 2026 edition put it at about 105,900.

metrics.metric_name: Hong Kong BN(O) visas, cumulative grants since January 2021
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, safe and legal (humanitarian) routes
metrics.notes: Out-of-country BN(O) visa grants since the route opened on 31 January 2021. 5,944 grants in the latest year, and grants have fallen in every calendar year since 2021: 75,579, 53,694, 28,168, 19,139 and 8,925.

metrics.metric_name: Afghan Resettlement Programme, cumulative arrivals
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, safe and legal (humanitarian) routes
metrics.notes: Breakdown: ARAP 20,407; ACRS 14,153; Afghanistan Response Route 4,468. In July 2025 the government confirmed the schemes were closing to new applicants; existing applications are still being processed. The three scheme figures sum to 39,028; the remaining 30 people are recorded under the programme with scheme name unknown, so the breakdown does not sum to the total. The Home Office states: 'Breakdowns exclude cases where scheme name is unknown but totals include them. Total resettled therefore may not sum.' Note also that the Home Office is inconsistent with itself on the third route: the topic page calls it the Afghanistan Response Route, its own table Res_01 calls it the Afghanistan Relocation Route.

metrics.metric_name: Total people resettled (all schemes), latest year
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending June 2026, safe and legal (humanitarian) routes
metrics.notes: Down 48% on the previous year (7,445). The Home Office states that 87% (3,352) arrived through the Afghan Resettlement Programme and 13% (488) through the UK Resettlement Scheme and Mandate Scheme.

metrics.metric_name: Returns from the UK (enforced plus voluntary)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, How many people are returned from the UK?
metrics.notes: The Home Office states this figure: 'Of the 40,605 returns from the UK in the latest year, three-quarters (76%) returned voluntarily and one-quarter (24%) were enforced by the Home Office'. It equals 9,669 enforced plus 30,936 voluntary, both printed in table Ret_01, which is a reconciliation rather than the origin of the figure; Ret_01 stays declared so that a correction to either component is still watched. COUNTS RETURN EVENTS, NOT PEOPLE: one individual returned more than once is counted more than once. EXCLUDES 18,646 refused-entry-at-port departures, which the Home Office counts separately, and adding them to this total is a common error. Both components are flagged provisional by the Home Office and so is this sum, the release stating that the latest seven quarters are revised each time. It was graded calculated until 3 August 2026 and briefly official the same day; provisional is the right destination, because meta.json defines provisional as official but flagged by the publisher as subject to revision, which is exactly what this is.

metrics.metric_name: Enforced returns from the UK
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, How many people are returned from the UK?
metrics.notes: Up 7% on the 9,077 in the year ending June 2025, which is the Home Office's own comparison. Return events, not unique people. Flagged provisional in table Ret_01.

metrics.metric_name: Voluntary returns from the UK
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, How many people are returned from the UK?
metrics.notes: Up 9% on the year ending June 2025, the Home Office's own comparison. Comprises assisted (11,048), controlled (6,151) and other verified (13,737) returns. Return events, not unique people. Flagged provisional.

metrics.metric_name: Refused entry at port and subsequently departed
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, How many people are returned from the UK? (table Ret_01)
metrics.notes: Counted SEPARATELY from the enforced-plus-voluntary returns total; down 11% on the previous year. Held here specifically to prevent the common misuse of folding port refusals into 'returns'. Flagged provisional.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum-related returns
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, How many people are returned from the UK?
metrics.notes: Up 14% on the year ending June 2025. Of which 3,841 enforced and 8,727 voluntary. A subset of total returns, not an addition to them. Return events, not unique people. THE PUBLISHER'S DEFINITION, added 10 August 2026 by the pre-publication review of /returns/: "Asylum-related returns relate to cases where there has been an asylum claim or further submission at some stage prior to the return." It is recorded because the page says the remaining returns involve people with no asylum claim at all, and that sentence rests entirely on this definition being drawn on whether a claim was EVER made rather than on why the person was returned. Nothing in this data layer established it before.

metrics.metric_name: People receiving an initial asylum decision
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, Asylum summary tables, table Asy_00a
metrics.notes: PEOPLE basis: main applicants plus dependants. Equals grants (42,394) plus refusals (73,478); EXCLUDES withdrawals (16,265). Up 2% on the previous year. Do not recompute the published 38% grant rate from these people-based figures, 42,394/115,872 gives 36.6% because the published rate is calculated on main applicants. This is a worked example of the people-versus-cases caveat.

metrics.metric_name: People refused protection at initial decision
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, Asylum summary tables, table Asy_00a
metrics.notes: PEOPLE basis: main applicants plus dependants. Up 23% on the year ending June 2025 (59,727). Around 40% of asylum appeals are allowed, so refusals at initial decision overstate final refusals.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum claims withdrawn (people)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, Asylum summary tables, table Asy_00a
metrics.notes: PEOPLE basis: main applicants plus dependants. Down 11% on the year ending June 2025 (18,174). Withdrawals are NOT part of the 115,872 people receiving initial decisions, and are excluded from the grant rate.

metrics.metric_name: Asylum claims with an administrative outcome (people)
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics year ending June 2026, Asylum claims and initial decisions detailed datasets, table Asy_D02
metrics.notes: CALCULATED by this project: the Asy_D02 pivot prints quarters and no year-ending total, re-checked on 27 August 2026. PEOPLE basis: main applicants plus dependants, all applicant types. Summed from that pivot over 2025 Q3 to 2026 Q2: 839 + 802 + 359 + 347. The pivot splits the same four quarters into void 1,633, other 375, suspended 287 and deceased 52, so voided cases are the great majority. The Home Office table notes say the category 'includes a small number of cases that were previously categorised as a withdrawal, as well as other administrative outcomes including voided and suspended cases'. Like withdrawals, these are NOT part of the 115,872 people receiving initial decisions and are excluded from the grant rate. The same four quarters give 73,478 refusals, 16,265 withdrawals and 42,394 grants, and a grand total of 134,484, which is how this figure's basis and period were confirmed. IT FELL BY MORE THAN HALF BECAUSE OF THE WINDOW, NOT A TREND: a 2025 Q2 spike of 3,807, mostly 3,131 voided cases, has dropped out of the twelve months.
